_about: Accepted CodeQL findings for .github/scripts/codeql_gate.py (playbook 9: CodeQL, own SARIF gate, medium and above).
One entry per finding, keyed on ruleId + fingerprint (SARIF partialFingerprints.primaryLocationLineHash), never per rule.
Every entry needs: language, ruleId, fingerprint, path, reason, acceptedOn (YYYY-MM-DD), acceptedBy.
The gate fails when an entry no longer matches a finding (stale), so remove entries when the code moves or the finding is fixed.
Re-triage at the new location before re-keying a fingerprint that an adjacent edit rehashed; never re-key on faith.

accepted.reason: hash_token hashes only random 256-bit secrets from secrets.token_urlsafe (invitation tokens, refresh tokens, API key secrets). A fast hash is the standard and correct choice for high-entropy random tokens; slow password hashing protects low-entropy human secrets, and the product has none (no passwords, ID-03). The low-entropy six-digit code uses a keyed HMAC instead (hash_code). Security review F30, docs/security/CHUNK1_AUTH_REVIEW_2026-09-19.md.
accepted.acceptedBy: Main build agent as a default, 2026-09-19 (owner may revert; see F30)

accepted.reason: set_refresh_cookie writes the refresh token into its cookie, which is the session design (D-06, ADR 0006): the cookie is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict and scoped to the auth path; the token is a random 256-bit secret the database keeps only as a hash, and it rotates on every refresh with replay detection (ID-S9). CodeQL reports the flow since c11-session-policy (ID-08) made the cookie's lifetime follow the session's absolute end.
